name: QAtelier document understanding evaluation
grounding_rule: Ground answers in the QAtelier document. Label external knowledge and inferences explicitly. Do not claim quantum advantage from accuracy alone.

questions.question: Give a concise, faithful summary of the QAtelier research plan. State the central research question, proposed contribution, experimental scope, and what would count as evidence for or against a useful quantum-adapter effect.
must_cover: low-data, out-of-distribution, and controlled high-order-correlation regimes
questions.citation_requirement: Cite the QAtelier document and distinguish its stated goals from interpretation.

questions.question: List the assumptions made by the QAtelier plan about the frozen representation model, the shared low-dimensional compressor, parameter matching, data regimes, training and selection, and execution on real quantum hardware. Mark each item as explicit or inferred.
questions.citation_requirement: Every explicit assumption should be traceable to a passage in the source.

questions.question: Reconstruct the proposed method as an ordered protocol: representation extraction, compression, quantum and classical adapter construction, training and model selection, evaluation regimes, and hardware validation. Include the comparison ladder and controls.
questions.citation_requirement: Cite the relevant QAtelier sections or passages for each major protocol stage.

questions.question: What are the strongest confounders, risks, failure modes, and falsifiers for the QAtelier claim? Prioritize risks that could make a quantum adapter look better for reasons unrelated to its inductive bias, and state the control or measurement that addresses each risk.
questions.citation_requirement: Separate risks explicitly discussed in the plan from evaluation recommendations.

questions.question: Create a citation and verification ledger for the QAtelier plan: identify five important externally verifiable claims, explain what evidence each claim needs, and mark whether the plan already supplies support or whether a paper, dataset, hardware, or implementation citation is still required.
questions.citation_requirement: Do not invent bibliographic details; use placeholders when the plan does not provide enough information.

questions.question: Find the most important mathematical expressions in the QAtelier plan. Transcribe each faithfully in plain text or LaTeX, explain the variables and the role of the expression in the research design, and mark any symbol that is uncertain or reconstructed.
must_cover: role in the hypothesis or protocol
questions.citation_requirement: Never silently normalize an unreadable equation; cite the relevant heading, page, or image location.

questions.question: Inspect the QAtelier DOCX for embedded images, diagrams, tables, or handwritten annotations. Describe what each visual contributes to the plan and cite its document location. If no such visual is present, say so explicitly rather than inventing one.
questions.citation_requirement: Use image, table, heading, or archive-member citations and flag visuals requiring human review.

questions.question: Propose the first three QAtelier experiments in dependency order. For each, specify the hypothesis, data/task regime, quantum and classical baselines, metrics, resource measurements, stopping or falsification rule, and the result that would justify moving to the next experiment.
must_cover: hardware validation or a justified hardware gate
parameter, runtime, shot, and energy/resource accounting
questions.citation_requirement: Anchor the experiment sequence in the plan and label any proposed extension as a recommendation.
